# Indonesia's captive power plants putting energy transition at risk, researchers say

By Reuters

January 27, 2026 1:05 AM UTC Updated January 27, 2026

Save article Indonesia's captive power plants putting energy transition at risk, researchers say

Smoke and steam billow from a coal-fired power plant in Suralaya, Banten province, Indonesia, July 11, 2020. Picture taken July 11, 2020. REUTERS/Willy Kurniawan/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

JAKARTA, Jan 27 (Reuters) - Efforts to decarbonise Indonesia's power sector have been put at risk by a faster than expected increase in the number of off-grid coal power plants and a lack of transparency when it comes to cutting their emissions, researchers said on Tuesday.
